title: Unstable angina and NSTEMI: risk and timing

nodes.text: Chest pain suggesting acute coronary syndrome (ACS): rest pain over 20 minutes, crescendo, new-onset or post-infarction
12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) within 10 minutes; draw troponin
nodes.detail: Repeat ECG every 15–30 minutes if pain continues.

nodes.text: ST elevation on ECG?
ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI): follow the STEMI pathway
Exclude other causes: aortic dissection, pulmonary embolism, pneumothorax, pericarditis
Very high risk?
nodes.detail: Refractory pain, shock, acute heart failure, life-threatening arrhythmia, mechanical complication, or dynamic ST-T change.

nodes.text: Aspirin 325 mg, heparin and ticagrelor; nitrate for pain. Do not wait for troponin
nodes.detail: No beta-blocker in shock or heart failure.

nodes.text: Angiography within 2 hours at a PCI centre
nodes.detail: PCI = percutaneous coronary intervention. Not PCI-capable: transfer at once.

nodes.text: Aspirin 325 mg, then 75 mg daily
P2Y12 inhibitor: ticagrelor first; prasugrel only if PCI planned; clopidogrel if neither suits
nodes.detail: Ticagrelor 180 mg, then 90 mg twice daily. Avoid after brain bleed or with active bleeding.

nodes.text: One anticoagulant: fondaparinux, enoxaparin or unfractionated heparin
nodes.detail: Fondaparinux 2.5 mg daily (not if creatinine clearance below 20). Enoxaparin 1 mg/kg twice daily.

nodes.text: Metoprolol unless heart failure, shock risk or AV block; atorvastatin 80 mg unless liver disease
nodes.detail: Nitrate for pain unless systolic BP below 90 mmHg.

nodes.text: Serial high-sensitivity troponin at 0 and 1 hour
nodes.detail: Unclear: repeat at 3 hours. Conventional assay: repeat at 6 hours.

nodes.text: Troponin raised?
GRACE above 140, TIMI above 4 or dynamic ST-T change?
nodes.detail: GRACE and TIMI scores: see the score tables.

nodes.text: Angiography within 24 hours
GRACE 109–140 or TIMI 2–4?
Angiography within 72 hours
Angiography during this admission
GRACE above 140, TIMI above 4, dynamic ST-T change or recurrent pain?
Angiography within 24 hours
GRACE 109–140 or TIMI 2–4?
Angiography within 72 hours
Low risk: aspirin 75 mg, clopidogrel 75 mg, metoprolol and statin
Non-invasive test within 1 week: CT coronary angiography, treadmill or stress imaging
Recurrent pain, new ECG change, ejection fraction below 40% or positive test?
Refer for angiography and revascularisation
Discharge with secondary prevention and early review
nodes.detail: Pain-free, stable, ECG unchanged, troponin negative.
